dedupe_keys.name: itu t recommendation y 3090 digital twin network requirements and architecture

description: Recommendation ITU-T Y.3090 defines the requirements and reference architecture of a digital twin network, a virtual representation of a physical telecommunication network used to analyse, diagnose, emulate and control that network from data, models and interfaces in a real-time interactive mapping. It was approved by Study Group 13 on 13 February 2022 as edition 1.0 and is in force. Coverage: functional requirements (including collecting only the data that the topology and application need), service requirements such as compatibility across vendors, network types and applications, a three-layer architecture of physical network layer, network digital twin layer and network application layer, with data, model and management domains inside the twin layer, security considerations per layer, and an informative appendix of six use cases (operation and maintenance of very large networks, optimisation, faster innovation, fuller measurement, intent-based networking and security strategy drills). Format and access: a 26-page English PDF (about 0.8 MB) free from the ITU-T recommendations page, and a Word version for TIES account holders. Licence: copyright ITU, all rights reserved; the PDF is offered as a freely available item. Caveats: this is a requirements and architecture text with no data model, schema or reference implementation; the related IETF and ETSI work on network digital twins is separate and not covered here. Simulation uses: a shared vocabulary and layering for building and comparing telecom network digital twins used in resilience and what-if studies. Related records: commercial and open network twins such as VIAVI's network digital twin (platform-viavi-network-digital-twin) and BubbleRAN MX-DT (platform-bubbleran-mx-dt-network-digital-twin) implement this kind of system.
